questions.question: Two years ago, T was twice as old as P. P is thrice as old as R. In five years, P will be 29. What is the present age of T?
questions.solution:
Given: Two years ago, T was twice as old as P. P is thrice as old as R. In five years, P will be 29. 

According to the question,

Two years ago, T was twice as old as P.

 
• T - 2 = 2 × (P - 2); _________(i)

At present, P is thrice as old as R.

 
• P = 3 × R; ____________(ii)

In five years, P will be 29. 

 
• P + 5 = 29
 
• P = 29 - 5 = 24 years

Now, by substituting the age of P, we get,

 
• T - 2 = 2 × (P - 2)
 
• T - 2 = 2 × (24 - 2)
 
• T - 2 = 2 × 22
 
• T = 44 + 2
 
• T = 46 years

Hence, the present age of T is **46 years.**

questions.question: What is the ratio of money held by public in currency to that they hold in bank deposits called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Currency Deposit Ratio.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Currency Deposit Ratio is the ratio of money held by public in currency to that they hold in bank deposits.
 
• The currency deposit ratio shows the amount of currency that people hold as a proportion of aggregate deposits. ** **
 
• It reflects people's preference for liquidity.
 
• An increase in the currency deposit ratio leads to an Decrease in the money multiplier effect. ** **
 
• An increase in deposit rates will induce depositors to deposit more, thereby leading to a increase in the Cash to Aggregate Deposit ratio. This will in turn lead to a fall in Money Multiplier. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The proportion of the total deposits commercial banks keep as reserves are the Reserve Ratio.
 
• **Cash Reserve Ratio** is the fraction of money that banks must deposit with the RBI. Banks do not earn any interest on this amount.
 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio** is the fraction of the total deposits of a bank that must be kept in a liquid form.
 
 
• Banks can use this money to purchase Government Securities (G-Sec).

questions.question: A man lent out ₹14,000 at 5% and ₹19,000 at 6% simple interest per annum. His total income (in ₹) from the interest in 3 years is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Simple Interest = (P₁ × effective rate 1) + (P₂ × effective rate 2)

Effective Rate = Rate × Time

Total Interest = (14000 × 15%) + (19000 × 18%)

Total Interest = 2100 + 3420 = 5520

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal 1 (P₁) = ₹14,000, Rate 1 (R₁) = 5%, Time (T) = 3 years

Principal 2 (P₂) = ₹19,000, Rate 2 (R₂) = 6%, Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6b38849eb7537aaee3f625f076f630ce22661a3f277efb1397ac53e379d2dd3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI₁ = (14000 × 5 × 3) ÷ 100 = 140 × 15 = ₹2100

⇒ SI₂ = (19000 × 6 × 3) ÷ 100 = 190 × 18 = ₹3420

⇒ Total Interest = SI₁ + SI₂

⇒ Total Interest = 2100 + 3420 = ₹5520

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) after T years is given by A = P + SI = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Simple vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest is calculated only on the initial principal. In Compound Interest, interest is calculated on both principal and the accumulated interest of previous periods.

Effective Rate Method

For Simple Interest, the effective rate for T years is simply R × T%. Here, 5% for 3 years becomes a 15% flat interest rate on the principal.
